header.title: Registri Epistolarum: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Gregorius I Magnus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tmp1291.tmp1291.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:tmp1291.tmp1291.opp-lat: *albula* (literally 'a little white one') is an unidentified white stone, perhaps a pearl. 'condiatur', literally 'be seasoned', is rendered 'be commended'.

*canterma* is a rare word of uncertain sense, evidently a kind of spell or charm. The psalm reference is printed garbled (CXIXVIII); the verse is Vulgate Ps. 138:21. OCR damage read through, e.g. 'fustinet' as 'festinet', 'furtis' as 'fortis', 'Ner' as 'per'.

nodes.text: The most holy man Maximian, our fellow bishop, desiring to purge the Church of God of wicked men, was, as you know, laudably watchful over the life of the clergy. While he was vigilantly attending to their actions with pastoral care, he learned that some of them were stained with the sorcery commonly called *canterma*. These too, as your Love's letter has reported, he had placed in custody to be held. But since, our sins bringing it about, he was overtaken by death and could not punish the crime himself, it is necessary that your Love should hasten to investigate this with all exactness, and take pains to punish them according to the enormity of the deed, in the way you know that the bishop named above, if he were alive, could have been moved according to the laws by zeal for correction and justice in this punishment for God's sake. With all strength, then, and all urgency, let your Love take care in this case to show its zeal toward almighty God, and to show his enemies hostility by inflicting fitting punishments, so that you fulfil what is written: Did I not hate those who hated you, Lord, and pine away over your enemies? (Ps. 138:21). If, then, your Love is fired by this zeal, let punishment be shown on those who have forsaken God and done something against him by sorcery. But if it cannot rightly be carried out there, those who are such must be sent to us, provided, however, that what convicts them there without difficulty could be shown here. But since I think this impossible, strict and firm correction must be brought about there through you. I trust that you have the glorious man the lord Libertinus, the praetor, as your helper in such a matter, out of regard for almighty God. In this case, however, you ought by no means to have grown lenient, even if some secular judge could have stood against you as an adversary.

To our most excellent son King Adaloald, moreover, we have taken care to send phylacteries, that is, a cross with wood of the holy cross of the Lord, and a reading of the holy Gospel enclosed in a Persian case. To my daughter his sister, too, I have sent three rings, two with jacinths and one with an *albula* [a white stone], which I ask you to have given to them, so that our love may be commended to them by Your Excellency.
